source: Unmodified transaction traces from the locally retained BSC Extended block captures (erc20/balances/out/top50-full-holder-blocks, producer version 5, endpoint bsc.firehose.pinax.network:443 at capture time). Each fixture keeps the block header, hash, number and one TransactionTrace; other transactions, system calls and block-level records are omitted to keep files small.
extraction: Decoded with prost from the captured <height>.pb, filtered transaction_traces to the listed index, re-encoded. No field edits.
layout: tests/fixtures/bsc-reviewed-layouts.json (WBNB direct mapping at slot 3, runtime 0xb7d84205eaaf83ce7b3940c6beaad6d22790255e34a9a2b486aa8cdfff118fe6)
scope: Regression evidence for non-Transfer balance mutations (issue #22). These are saved-data tests of the Rust mapper, not packaged WASM execution or fresh RPC qualification.

cases.demonstrates: deposit() by a contract five frames deep; Deposit event only, no WBNB Transfer; the holder is resolved from the storage write, not the sender; the WBNB contract's native balance rises by the same wad
deposit() then full withdraw() by a router in one transaction; the holder ends at a known zero and is emitted as 0; the wrapper's native backing returns to its starting value
withdraw() by a contract that is not the sender; Withdrawal event only; the holder's balance word is debited and the WBNB contract's native balance falls by the same wad
reverted transaction (status 3) containing a Deposit event, a Transfer event and WBNB storage writes; nothing persists, no ERC-20 row and no WBNB native row is emitted

succeeded transaction whose reverted child frame (ordinals 778-779) repeats WBNB writes later persisted at 802-803; a WBNB call made through Permit2 debits a holder that is neither the sender nor the caller; one holder nets to a known zero
